summary: The bill amends the CARES Act by striking subsection (c) of section 4024, which eliminates the federal requirement that lessors provide notice to vacate.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the CARES Act solely by removing a notice-to-vacate requirement for lessors. It contains no appropriations, authorizations, or changes to federal expenditures, so it has no bearing on government spending levels.
The legislation makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection mechanisms.
No provisions address health insurance, medical care delivery, public health programs, or market-based healthcare reforms.
The bill is unrelated to firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions are present.
The bill does not address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No defense or military spending authorizations are involved.
The legislation contains no environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions.

Section 4024(c) of the CARES Act imposed a federal notice requirement before eviction during the pandemic. Striking this subsection removes a tenant protection that had been layered on top of state law. While housing stability can intersect with social safety-net policy, the change is narrow, temporary in origin, and primarily restores state authority rather than directly expanding or contracting welfare programs such as SNAP or cash assistance. The effect is therefore tangential.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
Eviction procedures are civil matters; the bill makes no changes to criminal sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation policy.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are included.
The bill neither authorizes new spending nor contains deficit-reduction measures.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ legal protections or exemptions.
Foreign assistance is not addressed.
The legislation contains no election administration or voting access provisions.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or platform oversight measures are present.
The bill does not alter labor standards, collective bargaining, or employer obligations.
No religious exemptions or civil-rights balancing provisions are included.
